questions.subtopic: Domain 2: Security & Compliance (Security Groups vs NACLs)
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the difference between a Security Group and a Network Access Control List (NACL) in Amazon VPC?
options: Security Groups are stateless firewalls operating at the subnet level; NACLs are stateful firewalls operating at the instance level
Security Groups are stateful firewalls operating at the instance level; NACLs are stateless firewalls operating at the subnet level
Security Groups support both ALLOW and DENY rules; NACLs only support ALLOW rules
Security Groups filter traffic at Layer 7; NACLs filter traffic exclusively at Layer 2
questions.explanation: Security Groups operate at the individual instance (ENI) level and are stateful: if inbound traffic is allowed, outbound response traffic is automatically allowed. In contrast, NACLs operate at the subnet boundary and are stateless: rules must be explicitly configured for both inbound and outbound traffic in numerical order.
